speaker: Doctor
text: I see you're experiencing wrist pain, fever, and skin lesions. To better understand what's causing these symptoms, can you tell me how long you've had these symptoms and if they have worsened over time?

speaker: Patient
text: 17-year-old male. The patient presents with a 3-day history of pain in his left wrist, which worsened this morning accompanied by chills and malaise. He recounts having a self-resolving left knee pain the previous week. Reports recent return from a camping trip in Minnesota. Sexually active with one female partner. No history of trauma to the wrist.

speaker: Doctor
text: That recent knee pain and your camping trip in Minnesota are very concerning clues. Can you describe the appearance of your skin lesions and exactly where on your body they are located? Also, have you noticed any redness or warmth specifically around the painful wrist joint?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Pain in the left wrist. I also have Chills, Malaise, Painless violaceous vesiculopustular lesions on both wrists and hands, Swelling and erythema of the left wrist, Severe tenderness to palpation and passive movement of the left wrist.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Erythema Infectiosum (Fifth Disease) with Reactive Arthritis.

REQUEST IMAGES: Photograph of skin lesions on wrists and hands.

The "slapped cheek" rash often associated with this condition may have appeared earlier; do you recall any facial redness or a rash on your trunk or legs? Also, have you noticed any joint swelling or pain in other joints besides your knee and wrist?
